expected_effect: After redeploying mongodb-geo at mongo:4.4.6 (the tag recorded immediately before the 06:52:47 platform-automation image update), the recreated mongod should complete startup instead of aborting: the Loki stream for {namespace="hotel-reservation",pod=~"mongodb-geo-..."} should stop emitting the initandlisten 'Shutting down' record with exitCode 62 and should instead reach a 'Waiting for connections' / listening line, and the pod's restart count should stop incrementing. The mongodb-geo alert that fired at 06:53:54 should clear. Note that mongodb-geo emits no span-derived metrics [tr_d1c94edb180d], so error-ratio/latency panels cannot confirm this — confirmation must come from the pod log tail and restart count, not Prometheus.
if_wrong: Falsified if, on 4.4.6, mongod still logs an initandlisten shutdown with exitCode 62 (or any non-zero startup abort) and the pod keeps crash-looping past the confirmation window — that would mean the abort is driven by something other than the binary version, e.g. the failure-admin-geo ConfigMap mounted at /scripts at 06:52:04 [tr_73ec19bd8628], which was never read, or by PVC content/permissions. Also falsified if the process starts but no caller traffic recovers, which would put the fault downstream of the database. The triggering assertion line before each shutdown was never retrieved, so exit 62's meaning here rests on convention rather than this environment's own error text; that is the main weakness in this proposal.
risk: If the diagnosis is wrong, this costs a container recreate on an already-dead service and, worse, buries the real trigger: re-pinning to 4.4.6 may make geo start while leaving a mounted fault-injection artifact (/scripts, failure-admin-geo) in place and unexamined, so the same failure can recur on the next pipeline run. If any 8.0-rc data had been written to geo-pvc, a 4.4.6 binary would itself refuse those files — the logs show a clean WiredTiger close with rollback-to-stable and no listening state reached, so this is unlikely but not excluded, and the failure mode would be an identical crash-loop at the older tag. This also diverges geo's image from the four sibling mongodb instances still on 8.0.14-rc0, leaving the deployment inconsistent until they are handled the same way.
blast_radius: One service. mongodb-geo's inbound callers in the hotel-reservation dependency graph see the connection reset while the container is recreated — but those callers are already failing, since mongod has not been reachable since 06:53:49 [tr_b6ac44351d92], so the marginal impact is near zero. This does not touch mongodb-rate, mongodb-user, mongodb-recommendation or mongodb-profile, which remain crash-looping on the same image and will each need their own decision; mongodb-profile in particular was never directly observed and its participation is inferred.
